extracted.intended_audience: Authors submitting NLP/ACL-area papers to ACL Rolling Review (ARR)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing, submitting, responding to reviews, resubmitting, and committing NLP/ACL-area papers to the ACL Rolling Review (ARR) platform. Covers scope, formatting, anonymity, author responses, review-issue reporting, resubmission and commitment procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is ARR right for your paper? (Scope / suitability)
rubrics_metrics.description: ARR provides reviews—and only reviews—for submissions. The standards expected are those of a traditional direct submission as a long or short main conference paper to ACL (or other major ACL conferences).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the CFP and venues page for scope and venue-specific rules. System demonstrations should NOT be submitted (they have separate review processes and different policies). If you intend to send to a specialized venue (CoNLL, SEM, INLG, etc.), check whether it's listed on the venues page; some venues are hybrid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission deadlines are firm
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a submission deadline every two months; deadlines are firm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See dates and venues. Submit at least one hour before the deadline in case of system instability. You may edit all aspects of your submission up until the deadline. After submission you must register authors within 48h (see penalties section).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting and submission templates
rubrics_metrics.description: The submission must adhere to the formatting in the submission templates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Templates are available (including an Overleaf template). Failure to adhere can lead to desk rejection; consult the submission templates before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of submission form and responsible-NLP checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are encouraged to review the submission form and the responsible NLP checklist which list questions asked during submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review the list of common problems to avoid desk rejection and use track keywords to choose the right track.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer sign-up requirement (starting May 2025)
rubrics_metrics.description: Starting in May 2025, all submitting authors have to also sign up as reviewers (deadline: 48h after the submission deadline).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether you receive assignments depends on qualifications and the submission pool; see incentives policy. After submission, authors must complete the author registration form within 48h of the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submissions made via OpenReview and anonymous preprint option
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions are made in OpenReview. At submission you may opt to have ARR publish your paper as an anonymous preprint; these remain anonymous during and after review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may remove an anonymous preprint by contacting the ARR editors. Submissions remain editable until the deadline; all authors will receive a confirmation email upon submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: No dual submission while under review
rubrics_metrics.description: As soon as you have submitted and until you receive the meta-review, the paper is considered under review by ARR and may not be submitted elsewhere during this period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After the meta-review is issued the paper is no longer under ARR review and may be submitted elsewhere; authors who withdraw after receiving meta-reviews may be misunderstanding this.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal rules and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: You may withdraw your submission while under review (before it receives a meta-review), but withdrawing more than 48 hours after the submission deadline makes the paper ineligible for resubmission in the next cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To withdraw, use the OpenReview interface. Withdrawal consequences: earlier reviewed versions become ineligible for commitment; restoring withdrawn submissions is required to resubmit; if the paper had even one review it counts as a resubmission and must be disclosed with explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desk rejection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: A submission may be desk rejected if it does not adhere to the CFP (out of scope, violates technical submission requirements, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Desk rejection can occur at any point in the review cycle, even after initial reviews or a meta-review, if a technical violation is discovered. Desk-rejected versions do not count as prior submissions for the next cycle. Consult the list of common problems to avoid desk rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties for irresponsible reviewers and chairs
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers or area chairs who receive assignments but act irresponsibly will not be allowed to (re-)submit or commit their work during the current and next ARR cycle; their teams will have to sit out a cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should ensure all co-authors are aware of this policy and complete author registration on time. If assigned reviews or metareviews, they must be completed on time; in emergencies notify chairs via the emergency declaration form. See ARR incentives policy for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of the author response
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of the author response is to clarify misunderstandings or correct factual inaccuracies in reviews; ARR author responses have different goals than conference responses because ARR only provides reviews (no accept/reject decision).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If criticisms are minor misunderstandings, respond to clarify. For clarity objections or major issues, consider revising and resubmitting. If reviewers have unfair objections, consider resubmitting and requesting different reviewers; you can cite ARR reviewer guidelines if arguing reviewer guideline violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author response content restrictions (no links/images)
rubrics_metrics.description: Author responses must be text-only; no external links or images are allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violation of this rule will lead to desk rejection. Use 'Official Comment' in OpenReview to add responses. Back-and-forth conversations are allowed but must remain text-only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope for new experimental results in author response
rubrics_metrics.description: It is OK to present new experimental results that are in direct response to a reviewer's question, provided they are minor add-ons to existing experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed examples: a new ablation, a different hyperparameter setting, or an additional baseline comparison. Disallowed: unsolicited new results or substantial additional work (e.g., results of new improved models).

rubrics_metrics.name: Author response length and focus expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep author responses concise and focused on the main issues that significantly impact assessment; ACs are asked to read at least 2 author responses per review thread but are unlikely to read more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The recommended visible discussion length at ARR is maximum 2 author responses per review thread. Long back-and-forths are not helpful; focus on main points and clarifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction etiquette and non-response handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are not obligated to respond to author comments; authors should avoid flooding reviewers/ACs with reminders, which is likely to annoy ACs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a reviewer does not respond, flag non-response using the review issue report form. Do not repeatedly press reviewers to raise scores; it is not automatically grounds for flagging to ACs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review issue reporting (I1–I12)
rubrics_metrics.description: After the author discussion period, authors can report review issues via a form listing 12 issue types (I1–I12) to notify ACs about common review problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the mechanism only when the reviewer has not done due diligence; provide justification. Most issue types are referenced in ARR reviewer guidelines for easy lookup. The meta-review form includes checkboxes for ACs to indicate whether reported issues were considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-review issue reporting (MI...)
rubrics_metrics.description: Starting December 2024, it's possible to report issues with meta-reviews for procedural issues or serious violations of ARR policies (MI types).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mechanism is not for contesting reasonable differences of perspective. MI3 reports should be backed up by references to specific guidelines/policies. Reports are seen by senior area chairs and program chairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Options after final reviews (choices are mutually exclusive)
rubrics_metrics.description: After receiving final reviews and a meta-review, authors can: (a) quickly address feedback and submit to the next ARR deadline (~1 week), (b) spend more time and submit to a later deadline (2+ months), (c) commit the reviews to an ARR venue for an acceptance decision, or (d) submit for direct (non-ARR) review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These options are mutually exclusive (e.g., you cannot submit a revision and simultaneously commit to a venue). See CFP for rules on dual submissions and venue-specific policies (e.g., TACL waiting periods).

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding review outcomes vs acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer feedback and scores do not directly indicate whether the paper will be accepted when committed to a venue; reviews that are overall very positive are more likely to lead to acceptance, but there are no guarantees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different venues have different qualitative thresholds and editorial priorities. See ACL'23 report sec. 7 for analysis of how reviews and meta-reviews affected decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contacting reviewers for collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reviewer is helpful and you want to reach out for collaboration, contact the ARR editors who will reach out on your behalf to the reviewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the forum link and reviewer ID to editors@aclrollingreview.org; editors will contact the reviewer and put you in touch if the reviewer agrees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission required materials
rubrics_metrics.description: To resubmit, submit the same information as initial submission plus: (1) the link to your previous submission, (2) an explanation of revisions responding to previous reviews, and (3) preferences regarding reviewers and meta-reviewer (same or new).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The explanation of revisions should summarize changes and include point-by-point responses to weaknesses and suggestions. The same submission templates and page limits apply to resubmissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation of revisions content and format
rubrics_metrics.description: The explanation of revisions should summarize changes and include a point-by-point response indicating how you addressed each weakness and suggestion (or justify not doing them).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit as a PDF; you may include a color-coded version of the paper to show changes. Use different colors for content that is new vs content moved from other parts of the paper to aid reviewers and ACs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission frequency and page limits
rubrics_metrics.description: You can resubmit a paper multiple times; submission requirements are the same as for the first round (4-page limit for short papers, 8 pages for long papers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect diminishing returns after the first couple of rounds. If a paper was accepted for publication in one venue, you may still resubmit to another as long as you have not accepted the publication offer.

rubrics_metrics.name: What qualifies as a new submission
rubrics_metrics.description: A paper presented as a new submission must be on a sufficiently different topic such that prior reviews no longer apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minor reframing, improving methods, or adding baselines/analysis usually does not qualify. A paper previously submitted but not acknowledging the previous version will be desk rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to request new reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Request new reviewers if previous-round reviews lacked expertise or engagement with your topic; if previous-round reviews were constructive, consider asking for the same reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ARR generally accepts such requests, but expects papers to be revised based on earlier reviews. New reviewers will not see prior reviews initially; they see them only after submitting their own review (new since Aug 2023). New reviewers are instructed to form their own view rather than focus primarily on revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectations for repeat reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeat reviewers or substitutes focusing on the previous round are instructed to evaluate whether the revisions adequately address earlier weaknesses and are discouraged from raising new issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They may raise new issues only if revisions produced contradictory findings or questionable results not present earlier. In rare cases, ACs can recommend that a specific low-quality review be removed from view.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment process
rubrics_metrics.description: Commitment occurs through a submission form set up by the venue that asks for the ARR URL; after the commitment deadline ARR provides the reviews to the venue, which then makes acceptance/rejection decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different venues have different commitment deadlines and processes. ARR does not restrict committing to multiple venues, but venues may disallow dual commitments. The commitment phase ends when the paper is no longer under consideration by any venue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of commitment and camera-ready submission
rubrics_metrics.description: If you receive a decision of acceptance and submit the camera-ready, you accept the publication offer and the paper can no longer be withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If rejected, you can withdraw and return to Step 3 and possibly resubmit. There are no guarantees that resubmission will yield a better outcome; different venues may reach different decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of optional 'response to the meta-review' field
rubrics_metrics.description: If the venue provides an optional response-to-meta-review field, use it only as needed (optional).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Possible uses: summarize revision history; outline changes you commit to for camera-ready; summarize serious procedural issues with a link to a confidential comment. Be brief and avoid litigating minor issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: ACs may raise new issues in the meta-review
rubrics_metrics.description: Area Chairs are allowed to bring up new issues in the meta-review if they strongly believe reviewers missed something serious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a new issue is raised only in the meta-review and you believe an author response resolved it, flag it (MI5) and provide a link to the comment; ACs are not expected to mention every detail of the discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Camera-ready instructions are venue-specific
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the paper is accepted by a venue, preparation and submission of the camera-ready is handled by that venue, not ARR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the venue's Program Chairs or Publication Chairs for camera-ready formatting and Anthology timing questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do dissertations count as prior publications?
rubrics_metrics.description: University dissertations and theses do not count as prior publications for the purposes of ARR submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer the preprint question focusing on deanonymization risk rather than publication channel. Withdrawn publications that reveal authors' names also count as preprints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations section guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Limitations should focus on the soundness of the study and methodological caveats the reader should be aware of when interpreting results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss convenience sampling (models, languages, data), possible confounding factors (e.g. LLM test data contamination), practical limitations (compute costs), and directions of generalizability not tested. State clearly what was done, scope of claims, where results may not hold, and what future work would be needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contributing to the anonymized paper/review dataset (consent)
rubrics_metrics.description: The submission form asks if you agree for anonymized metadata associated with your submission to be included in a publicly available dataset; metadata is included only if both you and reviewers agree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission and review texts are handled separately. If you wish to donate your paper draft with associated review reports, you will be contacted after acceptance; in the forum, use the 'License Agreement' button to select what to contribute and sign digitally. Only one author needs to sign on behalf of all co-authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to get help / who to contact
rubrics_metrics.description: For further questions about ARR submission, contact support at aclrollingreview.org or editors for reviewer-contact requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the ARR guide for OpenReview submissions and the CFP for qualification requirements for reviewers. Use support channels rather than repeatedly contacting ACs about procedural matters.
